What do you like best about NetHunt CRM?

We've been using NetHunt for a while now and the experience has been largely positive.

The team is responsive and genuinely tries to accommodate feature requests, which matters when you're building on top of a platform.

The flexibility is the main draw. With the right setup, you can get a lot out of it (automated workflows, custom reporting, and integrations with other platforms via webhook.) That last part is underrated; being able to connect NetHunt to external tools without needing a full developer build has opened up a lot for us.

It's also easy to tailor to your actual business process rather than adapting your process to the tool. For a team that wasn't coming from a strong CRM culture, the interface was intuitive enough that adoption wasn't a battle. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What do you dislike about NetHunt CRM?

The flip side of the flexibility is that some things require workarounds rather than native features (helper fields, workflow logic, and so on.) But there's an argument that this is inherent to the trade-off: a CRM with every feature built in natively is also a more complex CRM to learn.

NetHunt's simplicity is part of why our team picked it up quickly, and you probably can't have both. For teams where adoption is a real concern, that's worth keeping in mind. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is NetHunt CRM solving and how is that benefiting you?

NetHunt handles email and WhatsApp tracking automatically, so activity is logged without the rep having to do anything. That alone removed a lot of friction.

Beyond that, we've been able to automate the repetitive end of sales outreach, marketing lead capture, lead nurturing, and lead assignment things that would otherwise fall through the cracks. Sales performance tracking is also centralised now, which makes reporting and accountability much easier to manage. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

![Easiest CRM Software for Small Business: 10 Simple CRMs Ranked](https://nethunt.com/blog/content/images/size/w2000/2025/03/easiest-crm-main-pic.jpg)

The easiest CRM is one your team can understand quickly and continue using once the novelty wears off. For most businesses, that means contacts are easy to organize, the pipeline reflects the real sales process, communication appears in one history, and follow-up reminders happen automatically.

**NetHunt CRM** is the easiest pick for Gmail and Google Workspace teams — the CRM runs inside your inbox, so there's no new interface to learn. **Less Annoying CRM** wins on pure simplicity: one price, four tabs, nothing extra, and the highest ease-of-use score in the entire CRM category. **HubSpot CRM** is the best free starting point for beginners who need something functional on day one without a credit card.

The full comparison below covers all ten tools and explains where each one feels simple — and where additional setup or cost enters the picture.

## What is the easiest CRM to use?

An easy CRM is customer relationship management software that a team can set up quickly and use with minimal training. It keeps contact data, communication history, deals, tasks, and follow-ups in one place. The best easy CRMs have a clear interface, customizable records and pipelines, simple no-code automation, familiar integrations, and transparent pricing. They reduce routine data entry while giving every team member a clear view of each customer and the next action required.

## **What Makes a CRM Genuinely Easy to Use? Key CRM Features That Actually Matter**

"Easy to use" gets thrown around in every CRM pitch. In practice, it comes down to four things.

- **Fast setup.** A genuinely easy CRM should be operational within an hour — contacts imported, pipeline configured, first email tracked. If you need a consultant or a week of IT time, the tool has already failed the test. Small teams in particular can't afford days of onboarding before getting any value.
- **A familiar interface.** The fastest onboarding happens when the CRM lives inside a tool your team already uses every day — tools your team already uses like Gmail, Google Calendar, or Slack. That's why Gmail-native CRMs have such low learning curves: there's no new tab to open, no new mental model to build. Easy to set up is not the same as easy to understand long-term, and the best simple CRMs deliver both.
- **No-code automation.** Saving time through [CRM automation](https://nethunt.com/sales-automation) shouldn't require a developer. The best simple CRM tools let you build if-this-then-that workflows from a visual editor in minutes. When follow-up sequences run themselves, your team focuses on selling instead of updating records.
- **Honest pricing.** Hidden costs, mandatory onboarding fees, and feature-gating on basic functionality all make a CRM harder to use in practice — even if the interface looks clean. A simple CRM should be simple to buy, not just simple to navigate. When you look for a CRM, pricing transparency is as important as the feature list.

## **How We Evaluated the Best Simple CRMs: Our Methodology**

Each of the 10 CRMs below was scored on 7 criteria using a 0–10 scale, for a maximum score of 70 points. The weighting reflects what matters most for ease of use, not overall CRM power. This is how we determine the best simple CRMs — not by feature count, but by how well each tool removes friction for small business teams.

Note: scores are our editorial assessment based on hands-on research and verified user reviews. The order of products in the list (NetHunt first) is set editorially and is independent of scores.

## **The 10 Best Easy CRM Platforms: Full Reviews**

### **1\. NetHunt CRM — Best Simple CRM for Gmail Teams**

**G2:** [4.7/5 (280+ reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/nethunt-crm/reviews) · **Capterra:** [4.8/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/160787/NetHunt-CRM/) · **Starting price:** $24/user/month (billed annually) · **Free trial:** 14 days

NetHunt CRM is built entirely inside Gmail. Not as a sidebar — as a full CRM layer embedded in your inbox. Contacts, pipelines, automations, and reporting all live where your team already spends most of their working day. For teams running on Google Workspace, this is the simplest CRM setup possible: there's genuinely nothing new to learn.

That design decision is the single biggest driver of easy adoption. Most CRM rollouts fail not because the tool is bad, but because reps don't open it. NetHunt removes that friction by making the CRM the same tab as email — which is why businesses using NetHunt report onboarding new sales reps up to three times faster than with standalone CRM software.

Since 2015, NetHunt has built a strong reputation as a [simple CRM for small business teams](https://nethunt.com/crm-for-small-business). It supports multi-channel communication across [WhatsApp](https://nethunt.com/integrations/whatsapp), Instagram, Facebook, and Telegram alongside email — all logged automatically to the contact record. This makes it a genuinely all-in-one CRM for teams that sell across multiple channels without wanting to manage multiple tools.

In 2026, NetHunt added official [MCP integration](https://nethunt.com/mcp-ai), allowing users to connect ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools directly to their CRM data. You can search records, update deals, and analyze pipeline performance through a plain-language prompt.

**Key features:**

- Full [Gmail](https://nethunt.com/integrations/gmail) and [Google Workspace integration](https://nethunt.com/integrations/google-workspace) (Contacts, Calendar, Meet, Looker Studio)
- Unlimited customizable [sales pipelines](https://nethunt.com/pipelines) with no-code field and stage editing
- Trigger-based CRM automation: deal stage changes, task creation, follow-up sequences
- [Multi-channel sequences](https://nethunt.com/multi-channel-sequences): email + chats in one workflow
- Automatic [lead capture](https://nethunt.com/lead-generation) from web forms, WhatsApp, Instagram, Intercom, and calls
- Integration with AI tools

**Pros:**

- Zero learning curve for Gmail users — the interface is already familiar
- Multi-channel outreach built in, not bolted on
- Strong automation on all paid tiers, including the entry plan
- Official MCP integration: manage your CRM through AI in plain language
- Deep Google Workspace sync (Calendar, Contacts, Meet, Looker Studio)

**Cons:**

- Requires Google Workspace — not suitable for Outlook or non-Gmail teams
- Automation features are unlocked on higher plans

### **2\. HubSpot CRM — Best Free CRM for Small Business**

**G2:** [4.4/5 (13,000+ reviews)](https://www.g2.com/products/hubspot-sales-hub/reviews) · **Capterra:** [4.5/5](https://www.capterra.com/p/152373/HubSpot-CRM/) · **Starting price:** Free / $9/user/month · **Free trial:** Free plan (no time limit)

HubSpot CRM is the default recommendation for beginners for good reason: you can start for free, set up a pipeline in under an hour, and have a working CRM before lunch. The free version is genuinely functional — contact management, deal tracking, email templates, and basic reporting are all included with no time limit and no credit card required.

The interface is clean and logically structured. HubSpot's visual pipeline with drag-and-drop deals is intuitive enough that first-time CRM users typically figure it out without reading documentation. The dashboard surfaces what matters — tasks, open deals, recent activity — without requiring any configuration first.

The main watch-out: meaningful sales automation lives behind the Sales Hub Professional ($90/user/month) plan, which also comes with a mandatory $1,500 onboarding fee. Teams that start with the free CRM often find themselves facing that jump sooner than expected.

Its strongest advantage is restraint. Users receive unlimited contacts, companies, pipelines, and custom fields without comparing multiple editions.

## **FAQ: Simple CRM Software for Small Business**

### What is the easiest CRM to use?

For Gmail and Google Workspace teams, NetHunt CRM is consistently the easiest — the CRM lives inside Gmail, so there's no new interface to learn. For everyone else, Less Annoying CRM scores highest on ease of use in the CRM category (9.8/10 on G2), and HubSpot CRM has the fastest onboarding for first-time CRM users.

### What is the best free CRM for small business?

HubSpot CRM offers the most functional free tier: unlimited users, contact management, deal tracking, and email templates with no time limit. Zoho Bigin is the best free option for solo operators (one user, core pipeline features). Less Annoying CRM has a 30-day free trial before the $15/month flat fee — no annual commitment required.

### What is the easiest CRM for Gmail users?

NetHunt CRM is the strongest pick — it embeds the entire CRM inside Gmail rather than adding a sidebar. Contacts, pipelines, automation, and multi-channel outreach all run within your inbox. Streak CRM is a good alternative for users who prefer a spreadsheet-style view. Copper CRM offers a well-designed sidebar with automatic data entry from email signatures.

### What is the easiest CRM for beginners with no tech background?

Less Annoying CRM is the most beginner-friendly option in this list: four menu tabs, one flat price, and a human customer support team. HubSpot CRM's free tier is a close second — the visual pipeline works without any configuration, and you don't need to read documentation to start tracking deals.

### Can a simple CRM scale as my business grows?

Yes, with the right choice from the start. NetHunt CRM supports teams from solo operators to 200+ users with progressively more powerful automation on higher tiers. HubSpot scales from a free CRM to a full marketing platform, though the price jumps significantly at the Professional tier. Zoho Bigin has a clear upgrade path to full Zoho CRM. Pick a tool with a visible tier structure rather than one built for a single use case.

### What are the key differences between a simple CRM and an enterprise CRM?

Simple CRMs focus on fast setup, intuitive pipelines, basic automation, email integration, and contact management at accessible prices. Enterprise CRMs — Salesforce, HubSpot Enterprise — add territory management, advanced AI, custom objects, and compliance tools built for organizations with dedicated admin teams. For most businesses under 100 people, enterprise-tier complexity lowers adoption rates without proportionate benefit. A simple CRM your team uses every day will outperform an enterprise CRM nobody opens.

### How much does easy CRM software cost for a small business?

Prices in this list run from $0 (HubSpot free, Zoho Bigin free for one user) to $49/user/month (Streak Pro). The most common entry price for a functional paid plan is $9–$15/user/month. NetHunt CRM starts at $24/user/month with a 14-day free trial. Less Annoying CRM is the simplest pricing model: $15/user/month, one plan, no annual commitment. When comparing options, always check which features are included in the entry plan — the headline price rarely tells the full story.
